paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the treasure is the gospel, and it sits in jars of clay on purpose. Paul says, "Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us." (2 Corinthians 4:7) So when you feel cracked, tired or a little blurry around the edges, that's not a sign the treasure is gone. I know a thing or two about being a worn-out container, and the power was never mine to begin with.

Paul doesn't pretend the clay is tough. He says they're "hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed," and "struck down, but not destroyed." (2 Corinthians 4:8-9) Hard things come, and they're real. But they don't get the last word, because the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus. (2 Corinthians 4:14) That's why Paul can say twice, "we do not lose heart." (2 Corinthians 4:1, 16)

So where do you put your eyes, baker? Paul says, "Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day." (2 Corinthians 4:16) He calls his troubles "light and momentary affliction," producing "an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison." (2 Corinthians 4:17) So keep your eyes on what is unseen, because it's eternal. (2 Corinthians 4:18) Keep serving, keep speaking and keep the ovens ready, because the treasure inside you is worth far more than the jar.
